title: Strait of Hormuz closes
description: Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, stops. Pipelines can reroute only part of the flow.

facts.text: About 20 million barrels per day flowed through the strait in 2024, around 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption and over a quarter of seaborne oil trade.
84% of the crude oil and condensate through the strait went to Asia; China, India, Japan and South Korea took a combined 69%.
Saudi and UAE pipelines could bypass about 2.6 million barrels per day.
India imports 88.7% of its crude oil.

affected.note: Largest exporter through the strait: 38% of Hormuz crude (5.5 million b/d).
A top destination for Hormuz crude.

title: Bab el-Mandeb shipping halts
description: The Red Sea chokepoint between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, the alternative route for Saudi oil to Asia, is closed to tankers.

facts.text: Houthi forces have seized islands near the strait and struck Saudi oil infrastructure and Red Sea shipping, stepping up pressure on global oil prices.
The strait is a key passage for Saudi oil shipments to Asia and serves as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.
India imports 88.7% of its crude oil.

affected.note: Houthi forces control islands near the strait.
Uses the strait to ship oil to its Asian markets.
An Asian oil importer that depends on imports for 88.7% of its crude.
